chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Husayn ibn al-Mundhir, from Umar ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him saying: 'Verily, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, did not leave anything which the community would need except that He revealed it in His Book and explained it to His Messenger (may the blessings of Allah be upon him and his family), and He made a limit for every thing, and He placed upon it an indication pointing to it, and He made a penalty upon whoever transgresses that limit.'

key_terms.الأمة: The Muslim community; here encompassing all who follow Islam
key_terms.حد (hadd): Dual usage: (1) a divinely set limit/boundary for every matter; (2) a prescribed legal penalty for transgression — the same word carries both meanings in this hadith
key_terms.دليل: Proof, indication, evidence — God's guidance that points to the correct path within each limit
key_terms.كتابه: His Book, the Quran — identified as the primary repository of divine guidance

ai.seo_question: What does al-Kafi say about the completeness of divine legislation in the Quran?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) asserts the completeness and comprehensiveness of divine legislation: God revealed all that the Muslim community would ever need in the Quran and through the Prophet's teaching, establishing a clear limit and guiding proof for every matter. The context reflects Shia theological concern with the sufficiency of Quran and Sunnah — and by extension, the Imam's authoritative explanation — as the complete source of religious law. The final statement that transgressors of the divinely set limits face prescribed penalties underscores that the legal framework is both comprehensive and enforceable.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Husayn Bin Al Munzir, from Umar Bin Qays, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘

Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High did not Leave anything which the community would be needy to except that He<sup>azwj</sup> Revealed it in His<sup>azwj</sup> Book, and Explained it to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and Made a Limit to be for everything, and Made evidence to indicate upon it, and Made a penalty to be upon the ones who exceed the Limit’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn Hadid from Murazim from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.

“Allah, the Most holy, the Most High has certainly revealed an explanation for all things even, by Allah, He has not left untold anything that His servants would need up to the Day of Judgment. He has done so, so that people would not be able to say if only so and so would have been said in the Quran. The fact is that He has already said it in the holy Quran.”
